name: BASELINE
expansion: Benchmark Atlas of Sanity-gated Event-classifier Losses: In-house vs. Nominal Evidence
tagline: The reference every other project is scored against

intro.problem: Every method in this program claims to improve the background estimate, but a claim is only as good as the baseline beneath it, and baselines drift: data files change, metrics are redefined between rounds, and a closure number is easy to quote under a different convention than the one it was measured with.
intro.value: A sanity-gated, hash-pinned baseline turns each later result into a measured difference rather than an argument, and measures in-house closure with the published definitions it claims to follow [@kasieczka2021][@cms2025tec].
intro.approach: A written run specification fixes everything before the first run: a data-health gate, eight loss families built from cross-entropy plus three penalty terms, five-fold training with early stopping, one grader whose metrics come from the literature, a dependence spectrum used only as a diagnostic [@kallenberg1999], and a pre-registered rule that locks one baseline per region.
intro.goals: The outcome is a locked baseline per detector region whose verdict comes from the six-item evaluation matrix, an append-only ledger of every run, and a record of which loss terms remove the dependence between the two scores and which only move it.

questions: Which combination of decorrelation and in-house closure terms gives the best held-out closure at an acceptable classifier cost, when every run passes the same gate and the same grader?
Do the closure terms remove residual dependence between the two scores, or relocate it into the corner of the plane where the signal region sits?
Where the data are too thin to test closure beyond the trained cuts, what can a baseline honestly claim?

components.name: Run specification
components.subtitle: Code truth, written before the runs
components.summary: One document defines a run from data to verdict; anything not written there is not part of BASELINE. Every definition is either cited to a published source or marked in-house, and every code path is named by its SHA-256. The run code checks those hashes at start and refuses to train on modified code unless the run is tagged as modified.

items.label: Run
items.detail: Identified by region, loss family, the three penalty weights and the seed; a cell is the set of runs that differ only by seed

items.label: Provenance
items.detail: Data hashes, code hashes, the resolved configuration, device and timing recorded with every run

items.label: Labels
items.detail: Signal is 1 and background is 0 in every file and every metric

items.label: Ledger
items.detail: One row per run, appended and never edited; a regrade keeps the replaced row in a separate file

components.name: Sanity gate
components.subtitle: Data health before any score
components.summary: An analysis-only gate runs on each region's training data before any training. It reports missing values, empty or constant columns, leakage columns, dead or compressed features, class balance and reproduction counts, and changes nothing except dropping invalid rows on request. A region passes only if none of the features the networks train on carries a leak flag, is missing, or is removed as empty; every other flag is recorded as information. Training refuses to start without a passing gate report made on the same data.

components.name: Loss families
components.subtitle: Three penalty terms, eight families, both regions
components.summary: Two networks score each event from separate feature sets, and binary cross-entropy on both is always on. Three penalty terms are added alone and in every combination, identically in the barrel and the endcap, giving eight families. The penalty code is taken byte for byte from the hash-sealed code genealogy.

items.label: F1 · BCE
items.detail: Two plain classifiers, no penalty: the control

items.label: F2 · + α DisCo
items.detail: Double DisCo: squared distance correlation of the two scores on background events only [@kasieczka2021][@disco2020]. It is the decorrelation reference every closure term is compared with

items.label: F3 · + β DNCn_QN
items.detail: In-house closure term: at cut pairs drawn inside the trained band, it penalizes the ABCD residual only where it exceeds its own statistical noise (hinged)

items.label: F4 · + γ DNC_FLR mk2.1
items.detail: In-house closure term, experimental: the same residual-over-noise statistic without a hinge, computed on the logits at deeper cut pairs

items.label: F5–F8 · combinations
items.detail: α+β, α+γ, β+γ and α+β+γ. Running two closure terms in one step is the only structural extension of the earlier trainer

components.name: Training
components.subtitle: Five folds, early stopping, GPU
components.summary: Five folds stratified on label and mass point, with the input scaler fitted inside each fold on training rows only. Early stopping uses a slice of the training rows, never the test fold, and selects the epoch on cross-entropy plus the DisCo term only, so a closure term can never choose its own epoch. Out-of-fold scores are saved as logits with probabilities alongside, with one checkpoint per fold; everything downstream reads only these files.

components.name: Unit tests
components.subtitle: Nine checks on the real data before any sweep
components.summary: The tests run on the analysis files themselves, never on synthetic data. Three of them gate, because the run code enforces the same conditions itself; the rest are information.

items.label: Code hashes (gates)
items.detail: Every canonical file and every package file matches its pinned SHA-256

items.label: Closure-term equivalence
items.detail: The reference implementation of the hinged closure term and the sealed unit give the same loss and gradient on real background scores

items.label: Label polarity
items.detail: Signal is 1 and background is 0 after loading

items.label: No leakage
items.detail: The scaler is fitted on each fold's training rows only, and training, selection and test rows are disjoint

items.label: Closure by hand
items.detail: The grader's closure equals a hand computation from the four region counts

items.label: Bit-exact reproduction
items.detail: The new trainer reproduces the earlier sweep trainer bit for bit on the CPU for the families both can run

items.label: GPU smoke test
items.detail: The full three-term family trains on the GPU with healthy losses

items.label: Data hashes (gates)
items.detail: Both input files match their pinned SHA-256

items.label: Region split (gates)
items.detail: Each region is cut from the shared files by its own flag column; unsplit data is refused

components.name: Grader
components.subtitle: Closure, contamination, separation, health
components.summary: One grader reads only the saved scores and computes every metric the same way for every run.

items.label: Closure
items.detail: %|nc|, the percentage by which N_B·N_C/N_D misses N_A in background [@kasieczka2021][@cms2025tec], on a grid of background-quantile cuts in steps of 0.05 (0.30–0.95 endcap, 0.30–0.80 barrel). Bands: trained up to 0.80 on both axes, tail from 0.90 (endcap) or 0.75 (barrel) on both axes, edge the rest. A cell is gradable only with at least 20 background events in region A and 10 in each control region. Reported per band, pooled and per fold, against a shuffle null, with the full signed map

items.label: Signal contamination
items.detail: δ in each control region and the normalized contamination r per mass point [@kasieczka2021]; information only, compared across cells, never used to gate

items.label: Separation
items.detail: Both networks' AUCs, the worst mass point, and background rejection at fixed signal efficiency of 30% and 10% among cuts that close within 10% [@kasieczka2021]

items.label: Significance
items.detail: Signal significance with the non-closure systematic in the form printed in [@cms2025tec]; relative only, reported and never used to select

items.label: Closure health (in-house)
items.detail: Pull of the region-A count against its propagated Poisson error with coverage, map coherence, roughness of closure along the grid, saturation of the scores, and fold-to-fold stability

components.name: Dependence spectrum
components.subtitle: Legendre diagnostic: what kind of dependence remains
components.summary: Closure says where on the cut plane the ABCD prediction fails, not what kind of dependence causes it. The spectrum adds that second axis for every run. Background scores are rank-transformed onto the unit square and their copula density is expanded in orthonormal shifted Legendre polynomials, the basis of data-driven rank tests for independence [@kallenberg1999]; each coefficient, scaled by its noise, is standard normal if the two scores are independent. Legendre rather than Fourier because ranks live on a bounded square with no periodicity: a periodic basis would put artificial dependence at the edges, which is where region A sits.

items.label: Bulk vs. tail
items.detail: Low-order modes are smooth, global dependence; high-order modes are localized and pile up in the corner where region A sits. A tail residual carried by high orders is one no penalty on the trained band can reach

items.label: Removal vs. relocation
items.detail: A term can improve closure in its own band by moving dependence into modes it does not see. The spectrum shows this as low orders down and high orders up with the total unchanged

items.label: Closure by cancellation
items.detail: Good closure at one cut can hide large low- and high-order parts of opposite sign; such closure fails at the next cut, and the verdict rules mark it FAIL

items.label: Over-forcing
items.detail: A closure term that drives the spectrum far above its reference cell has made the scores more dependent, not less; also a FAIL

items.label: Cut-free comparison
items.detail: The low- and high-order totals do not depend on any cut choice, so runs, families and regions compare on one scale

items.label: Limits
items.detail: Diagnostic only: the lock rule never reads it. The expansion is truncated at order 8 per axis in the endcap and 4 in the barrel, and low order means j + k ≤ 4. The truncation order and the low/high boundary are choices whose sensitivity is unchecked, and the smaller barrel sample may resolve nothing, which is an expected outcome rather than a failure

components.name: Sweep and lock
components.subtitle: Pre-registered selection
components.summary: Every run gets a verdict from health flags and spectrum rules, and a cell is OK only if every one of its seeds is OK. Selection uses OK cells only, by a rule written before the runs.

items.label: Stage A
items.detail: Each term alone, ten seeds per cell, plus the cross-entropy control. α ∈ {1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16} barrel and {2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32} endcap; β ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 3} both; γ ∈ {0.5, 1, 2, 4} barrel and {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2} endcap

items.label: Stage B
items.detail: Combinations around each term's best OK Stage A value, ten fresh seeds per cell: three by three windows for the pairs and two by two by two for all three terms, shifted inward at a grid edge

items.label: Lock rule
items.detail: Among OK Stage B cells, the lowest held-out-tail closure with both networks' AUCs no more than 0.01 below the control

items.label: Confirmation
items.detail: The locked cell and its references on fresh seeds, twenty in the barrel and sixteen in the endcap, plus a transfer run with the top third of background in missing transverse momentum held out

items.label: Verdict
items.detail: The locked baseline is the six-item evaluation matrix's verdict on the confirmation run: robustness, confirmation, deep tail, transfer, cut scan and signal cost, each with a paired, seed-by-seed pass rule and an event bootstrap

links.title: Barrel program
links.text: STAVE's barrel techniques are each scored against the barrel baseline locked here, with the same gate and the same closure measurement.

links.title: Architecture search
links.text: TRUSS rebuilds the plain, decorrelated and closure-term models; their reference points come from this baseline.

links.title: Joint background model
links.text: KERF's kernel and maximum-entropy background estimates are compared to the arithmetic ABCD prediction measured here.

open.text: In the barrel the cut grid ends inside the trained band, so the barrel's tail band is not held out from the closure terms. How to rank barrel combinations must be decided before the barrel lock.
The unhinged closure term trains on cut pairs that reach the first endcap tail cut, so for the families that use it the endcap tail is only partly held out.
Does the hinged closure term remove dependence, or move it from low- to high-order modes so that its band closes and the tail does not?
Does the unhinged term, trained at deeper cuts, reduce the high-order part of the tail residual where the hinged term does not?
Earlier sweep rounds used other closure definitions and grids, so their numbers are kept as history and cannot be compared with BASELINE number for number.
Reproducing published numbers with the BASELINE code path is deferred; the ledger keeps a place for it.

timeline.label: New data and background files; baselines re-run behind a minimal analysis-only gate
Refined sweeps of the decorrelation and closure terms in both regions
Pre-registered evaluation framework adopted for closure
Private repository created to hold the baseline record
Closure, error and plot canon written
Run specification written: eight loss families, one grader, a diagnostic dependence spectrum and a pre-registered lock rule
BASELINE code built to the specification; the sanity gate passes in both regions and every unit test passes on the real data
Stage A: each loss term alone, both regions
Stage B: combinations around the best single terms
Lock rule, then confirmation and transfer runs graded by the evaluation matrix
Hand the locked baseline to STAVE, TRUSS and KERF
